findings.text: Latch tree package offers insertion, removal and keyed search over a mirrored ordered tree. Updates affect both mirrors under a latched sequence discipline, while search observes one mirror selected by sequence parity and retries on concurrent update.

Resizable hash package offers RCU protected lookup, self locking fast lookup, list variant lookup, fast insertion, walk start, hashing helpers, bucket address helpers and a family of chain iteration helpers for locked and RCU contexts.

Table setup is exposed through wrapper macros that establish a lock class key and delegate to an underlying init routine, with allocation hook wrapping and separate spellings for plain and list tables.

Ordered node holds a combined parent plus colour word and two child links, with long alignment. Roots hold a top pointer; cached and linked roots add a leftmost pointer; linked nodes add predecessor and successor links. Empty roots are represented by null pointers.

Hash chain element holds a single RCU next link; list variant pairs that element with an RCU list next link. Compare argument bundles table pointer and key pointer. Hash parameters carry size hints, key geometry, limits, elasticity and shrink controls, plus hash and compare callbacks.

Table descriptor holds current bucket array pointer, key length, element ceiling, parameter copy, list mode flag, deferred work items, a mutex, a spin lock and an element count, with an optional allocation tag. List table wraps one descriptor. Walker tracks a list node and table pointer; iterator adds table pointer, cursor, list cursor, slot, skip and end flag.

Bucket array descriptor holds size, nesting level, random seed, walker list, RCU callback head, future table pointer used during resize, a lock dependency map, and a cache aligned flexible array of bucket heads.

Latch search descends one mirror using an ordering callback that yields less, greater or equal, follows left or right accordingly, and reports absence when the descent leaves the tree. Insertion descends with a less predicate to a vacant link and then links and rebalances there; erasure removes the indexed node from the selected mirror.

Bucket selection masks the hash with size minus one, so size is a power of two. Object address is recovered by subtracting a configured head offset from the chain element address. Empty or relocated chain ends use a tagged nulls marker derived from the bucket address; a low tag bit distinguishes such markers from real elements.

Key hashing prefers a caller supplied hash callback when available. Otherwise it uses a generic keyed hash, with a word oriented variant when key length is a multiple of four bytes. Object hashing prefers an object hash callback and otherwise hashes the embedded key bytes at a configured offset.

Growth and shrink decisions compare the live element count against fractions of current size and configured bounds. Thresholds near three quarters, three tenths, full load and an absolute maximum select expand, shrink or reject paths, with maximum size and minimum size acting as clamps.

Lookup scans one bucket chain with either a caller compare callback or a default memory comparison over configured key bytes at a configured offset. A scan that ends on a marker belonging to another bucket is repeated, and a newly published future table causes a restart on that table.

Fast insertion rejects duplicate keys for plain tables and chains duplicates for list tables by splicing the new list element ahead of the match. New distinct objects are prepended at the chain head. Chain length beyond an elasticity budget, detection of a pending resize, or load above full capacity diverts to a slow path; load above three quarters schedules background work.

Iteration helpers walk from a head until a nulls marker, advancing through RCU or bucket guarded next links. Entry variants translate each link to an enclosing object; safe variants prefetch the successor before the body runs. List helpers walk a null terminated list instead of a nulls terminated chain.

Per bucket exclusion uses a bit lock on the bucket pointer with interrupts saved across the critical section and a dependency map acquired for checking. Release restores interrupts and releases the map. A nested variant records a subclass. Locked store keeps the lock bit set while unlocked store publishes the new head and releases.

Readers use RCU: plain lookup and list lookup require RCU held, fast lookup acquires RCU internally, and bucket and link dereferences have RCU, mutex guarded and bucket guarded spellings. Latch readers sample a sequence value, read the mirror selected by its parity, and retry if the sequence changed; writers bracket the two mirror updates with begin, middle and end sequence operations.

Bucket address selection transparently handles nested tables: read, mutable and insert variants choose either direct indexing or a nested helper. Pointer decode masks off the lock bit and substitutes the bucket marker for a null value, with a likely present hint variant.

Latch update moves from quiescent to first mirror updated to second mirror updated and back to quiescent across the bracket operations. Readers that overlap an update observe a sequence change and repeat, so they only return results from a stable mirror.

Lookup starts on the current table, scans the selected chain, repeats the chain when its end marker moved, then observes the future pointer across a read barrier and restarts on the successor table when present, otherwise reports absence.

Fast insertion moves through hash, bucket resolve, lock, duplicate scan, limit checks, head link and background work scheduling. Missing bucket storage, pending resize, exhausted chain budget, absolute overflow and full load each divert to failure, unlock and retry, or slow path outcomes.
Latch mutation entries accept a node, a root and an operations bundle; lookup entry accepts a key, a root and the same bundle and returns a matching node or absence.

Hash lookup entries accept table, key and parameters and return object or list head; fast lookup needs no caller RCU. Fast insertion accepts table, object and parameters and maps outcomes to success, duplicate or error codes.

Calling RCU lookup variants without RCU held, dereferencing bucket links without the required bucket or RCU guard, or interpreting a bucket pointer without masking the lock bit and testing for a nulls marker can misread or corrupt chains.

Disabling the chain length safety control removes the diversion to the slow path on long chains, and inserting at high load without honoring the maximum element or full load checks risks unbounded chains or failed growth.
Chain scan budget before diverting to the slow path is sixteen.
